messages:
maria: Heads-up — profiler is showing divergent KV cache assimilation across hosted/dedicated/private after the kernel-selection change yesterday.

maria: quick summary: hosted shows high page counts and much higher fragmentation vs dedicated; private (on-prem) is somewhere in the middle but with memory growth on long contexts.

tom: can you drop the raw numbers/snippet? interested in peak/resident and frag%

maria: pasted from the trace collector (trimmed):
```
# kv-residency snapshot 2026-03-17T22:10Z
env=hosted   pages=1248  frag=21%  resident=13.9GB  peak=14.3GB  tail-allocs=1.2k
env=dedicated pages=812   frag=7%   resident=9.1GB   peak=9.5GB   tail-allocs=320
env=private   pages=967   frag=18%  resident=11.6GB  peak=12.9GB   tail-allocs=680
avg_token_seq_len: hosted=18k tokens ded=9k priv=12k
profiling-note: hosted workloads had continuous-batching enabled + tiled-kernel fallback disabled during run
```

anita: that lines up with my batch experiments — continuous batching increases temporal reuse but delays eviction, which inflates pages on hosts with larger multiplexed tenants.

anita: also noticed kernel-selection matters: the new vectorized kernel keeps larger per-request KV frames pinned longer (fast generation but larger resident). dedicated's kernel preference still uses smaller per-step kernels by default.

kevin: could VPC constraints / RPC MTU be causing extra fragmentation for private? sending larger KV pages over gRPC -> more split frames -> higher frag%?

oliver: we saw MTU-related reassembly affecting page boundaries before. worth checking network-level traces for on-prem setups.

maria: repro steps I used (easy):
1) run long-context stress: `bench/kv_stress --model gptx --tokens 65536 --concurrency 6`
2) enable continuous-batching vs disabled
3) collect `kv_residency.json` from /var/run/kvprof

maria: quick command to fetch policy from prod-ish envs:
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://ops.internal/api/kv/policy?env=hosted" | jq .
```

tom: any perf-regression traces? flamegraphs?

maria: yes — attached short flame from hosted canary (pasted):
```
# hot paths (hosted)
KV::pin_frame -> 34%
KV::evict_if_needed -> 6%
kernels::vector_tiled_step -> 22%
```

anita: compare that to dedicated run where tiled kernel is used less: `vector_tiled_step` is only ~8%, `kernel::step_small` is ~19%. explains lower resident.

kevin: mitigation ideas:
- tighten early-evict threshold for hosted (evict when resident_ratio > 0.65)
- enable periodic compaction pass every N minutes (cheap scan + coalesce)
- bias kernel-selection for long-context routes to smaller-step kernels on hosts with heavy multi-tenant loading

oliver: + check jemalloc background threads and tuning — fragmentation could be allocator-level rather than page-level. run `malloc_conf` toggles in canary.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment queued: `kvcache/tune-evict-hosted` -> started by @anita. build 2026.1797.001. ETA 12m.

maria: plan for next 48h:
- anita: run canary with early-evict + compaction (hosted only)
- kevin: run MTU & RPC reassembly trace on private on-prem hosts and dump pcap for suspicious flows
- oliver: run jemalloc heap profile on hosted canary
- tom: collect token-length histograms and per-route kernel selection logs

kevin: I can reproduce partial memory growth with `--mtu 1400` in dev onprem VM. will attach pcap.

anita: I'll push the evict tweak and compaction hook to canary now. keeping continuous-batching slower (batch_timeout=12ms -> 6ms) for the run.

maria: sweet. if this reduces resident by ~15% on hosted we can keep kernel-selection change but add the bias we discussed for multi-tenant hosts.

oliver: noted: add a telemetry flag that emits `kv_compaction:run=true/false` in traces so we can correlate.

tom: thanks everyone. @anita @kevin please cc me on logs. :thumbsup:

anita: will do.

kevin: on it — uploading pcap and jemalloc dumps to the thread bucket.

maria: closing loop: we'll reconvene tomorrow after 24h canary. if compaction + early-evict doesn't fix hosted, fallback is to revert kernel-selection for hosted only.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary finished: `kvcache/tune-evict-hosted` -> status=success (rollout=10%)."
